data.narrative:
DiamFab is a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Khaled Driche, Gauthier Chicot, and Ivan Llaurado, having raised €8.7M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductors peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage companies in Chips & Semiconductors, though the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints for robust statistical comparison.

Of three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using total raised (€8.7M, ~$9M) as a value proxy and applying a typical 2.5x Seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier yields an implied valuation of $22M. Peer-median triangulation was inapplicable due to insufficient narrow peers meeting stage and tier filters within the semiconductor sector. Public-comp anchoring, while supported by a 21.5x median P/S across the three public comparables, cannot be executed absent DiamFab's revenue, which private companies typically do not disclose.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $18M to $25M, centered on $22M. This range reflects the single methodological input and carries material uncertainty. Key sensitivities include DiamFab's actual revenue run-rate (if any), patent/IP defensibility relative to named peers (Cerebras, SambaNova, Etched), and market timing within semiconductor cycles. A fuller valuation would require either disclosed or modeled revenue, or a materially expanded private peer set at identical stage and capital scale.
